answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use graduated trust limits: a new identity starts with tiny transaction caps, like a reef that grows slowly on basalt rather than appearing overnight. Caps rise only after a record of completed, peer-verified jobs, and that record cannot be copied onto a fresh identity. An attacker spawning thousands of fakes must therefore pay the real cost of weeks of genuine work per identity, since no fable shortcut conjures reputation from nothing; honest agents earn larger limits only by delivering value.
